title: Pope's own orchestra and the drummers
summary: Pope played 18 years with Holman's orchestra, then formed Hoop's Dreamland Serenaders of eight or nine for society dances; the drum setup is discussed.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: stuff you used the same brass band lineup? That same brass band lineup. 14 pieces inside of

14, that's right. Of course in the latter days I organized my own orchestra and we had another orchestra by the name of Holman's. Holman. Orchestra, yes. And I played with him 18 years and after that I organized my own as known as Hoops Dreamland Serenators. How many were in that about? Well we had an average around eight to nine. Eight to nine. Did you use the bass or piano or guitar or anything in those? Well yeah we had the guitar, we had the bass, the piano, trumpet, three saxophones and drums. And for years I attended principal work in Mobile. All the big society dances out of town I played all those dances. That's what used to band all the time. Did you play mostly for music or did you have ear or head arrangements? Mostly by music. Mostly by music. Sometimes we'd pick up something very popular by air and we'd done pretty well with that. Did you add a little bit to it? That is sort of as they say, douse it up or make it raggy? Well we did. We did do that. We made it a little raggy as you say.
I wondered when the full band played they used two drummers inside. That's right, two drummers. One fellow hitting the bass drum. You used the bass drum for dancing too?
Well we had track drums then. We called them back to the band. I don't know what you call them now.
Now on your parade did the bass drummer play a cymbal to one hand?
That's right. They have cymbal, lift head and... Use a wire meter. That's right.
Like they... We used all those kinds of things.
